MISO accelerates new generation and storage projects with fifth ERAS cycle

7.3 GW of proposed capacity will strengthen reliability and meet growing demand

For Immediate Release

September 8, 2026

Media Contact

McKenzie Barbknecht

CARMEL, Ind.
 — MISO is accelerating its efforts to help bring new generation online quickly with the 
fifth cycle of projects
 to be evaluated under the Expedited Resource Addition Study (ERAS) process. These projects will reinforce reliability and support economic growth across the region.

This cycle includes 15 proposed projects totaling approximately 7.3 gigawatts (GW) of new capacity. The portfolio spans MISO’s North, Central and South regions and includes a mix of natural gas, solar, wind and battery storage resources that are expected to be in service by 2029.

“The MISO region is undergoing rapid change, with electricity demand rising at a historic rate,” said Aubrey Johnson, MISO’s Vice President of System Planning and Competitive Transmission. “Each ERAS cycle is helping us to bring reliability critical generation online faster while we work toward long-term improvements in the interconnection process.”

The fifth study cycle will include the following ERAS projects:

Bayou Point Combined Cycle (NextEra Energy Capital Holdings) – 750 megawatts (MW) of new gas generation in Louisiana

Calcasieu Parish Combined Cycle (Entergy Louisiana) – 767.7 MW of new gas generation in Louisiana

Crosley Energy Storage (NextEra Energy Capital Holdings) – 400 MW of new battery storage in Indiana

DOUBLEC Energy Center (DOUBLEC Energy Center LLC) – 400 MW of new solar generation and 400 MW of new battery storage in Arkansas

Little Rock Wind Project (Little Rock Wind Project LLC) – 300 MW of new wind generation in Minnesota

Malden Battery Energy Storage System (NIPSCO) – 600 MW of new battery storage in Indiana

Merom Energy Storage (NextEra Energy Capital Holdings) – 500 MW of new battery storage in Indiana

Point Coupee Combined Cycle (Entergy Louisiana) – 377 MW of new gas generation in Louisiana

Rapides Parish Combined Cycle (Cleco Power) – 756 MW of new gas generation in Louisiana

Sandcut Energy Storage (NextEra Energy Capital Holdings) – 350 MW of new battery storage in Indiana

Steamboat Energy Storage (NextEra Energy Capital Holdings) – 500 MW of new battery storage in Louisiana

Sullivan County Combined Cycle (Maple Creek Energy) – 641.8 MW of new natural gas generation in Indiana

Tradewater Energy Storage (NextEra Energy Capital Holdings) – 155 MW of new battery storage in Kentucky

Trotman Energy Center (Trotman Energy Center LLC) – 400 MW of new gas generation in Indiana

Since the launch of the ERAS program, 58 projects representing nearly 29 GW of proposed capacity have been or will be studied. Of these, 38 projects representing approximately 18 GW of proposed capacity have advanced to completed generator interconnection agreements, with an additional 5 projects representing approximately 3 GW of proposed capacity nearing completion. The program is capped at 68 projects and will sunset in 2027.

About MISO

Midcontinent Independent System Operator (MISO) is an independent, not-for-profit organization that delivers safe, cost-effective electric power across 15 U.S. states and the Canadian province of Manitoba. 45 million people depend on MISO to generate and transmit the right amount of electricity every minute of every day. MISO is committed to reliable, nondiscriminatory operation of the bulk power transmission system and collaborating with all stakeholders to create cost-effective and innovative solutions for our changing industry. MISO operates one of the world’s largest energy markets with more than $53 billion in annual gross market energy transactions.
